s1.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with gastrointestinal symptoms and a palpable mass
salient_findings: Palpable tender mass in the right hypochondrium
key_facts: Visible mass in the right hypochondrium
Tender 4×5 cm mass with localized rigidity
No air–fluid levels on erect abdominal radiograph
No free intraperitoneal air on erect abdominal radiograph
Abdominal ultrasonography and CT scan consistent with small-bowel intussusception

raw.syndrome_frame: Acute abdominal pain with gastrointestinal symptoms and a palpable mass
salient_findings: Palpable tender mass in the right hypochondrium
key_facts: Visible mass in the right hypochondrium
Tender 4×5 cm mass with localized rigidity
No air–fluid levels on erect abdominal radiograph
No free intraperitoneal air on erect abdominal radiograph
Abdominal ultrasonography and CT scan consistent with small-bowel intussusception

shortlist.label: Intussusception
shortlist.why_kept: Abdominal ultrasonography and CT scan consistent with small-bowel intussusception

shortlist.label: Intestinal polyp
shortlist.why_kept: Visible mass in the right hypochondrium and abdominal pain

shortlist.label: Meckel's diverticulum
shortlist.why_kept: Gastrointestinal symptoms and a palpable mass

shortlist.label: Inflammatory bowel disease
shortlist.why_kept: Loose stools, abdominal pain, and weight loss

raw.rationale: The patient's symptoms, including abdominal pain, vomiting, and a palpable mass, combined with imaging findings of small-bowel intussusception on ultrasonography and CT scan, strongly support this diagnosis.

rejected.label: Intestinal polyp
rejected.why: While possible, the presence of a palpable mass and intussusception on imaging makes this less likely as the primary cause.

rejected.label: Meckel's diverticulum
rejected.why: This condition could cause abdominal pain and vomiting, but the specific imaging findings of intussusception point more directly to intussusception.

rejected.label: Inflammatory bowel disease
rejected.why: The acute presentation and specific findings of intussusception are not typical for inflammatory bowel disease, which usually has a more chronic course.

rejected.label: Gastrointestinal stromal tumor
rejected.why: This is less likely given the acute presentation and the specific imaging findings consistent with intussusception rather than a solid tumor mass.
